messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan.park@clearguide.ai>, Clara Gomez <clara.gomez@clearguide.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Clarifying p95/p99 targets and test scope

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an actionable plan for the performance qualification (p95/p99 end-to-end):

What we discussed / still need from ClearGuide:
- Target SLOs you consider acceptable (p95 and p99 end-to-end, including network / client-to-API).
- Representative traffic profile: average QPS, expected peak QPS, typical concurrency (both request/response and long-lived streaming sessions).
- Streaming specifics: chunk size (tokens per chunk), average response length, do you use keep-alive streaming sessions / multiplexing?
- Token / sequence lengths for worst-case flows (max prompt + response tokens).
- Any geo/regional routing requirements (we have regions in us-west/us-east/eu).
- Current provider artifacts helpful for benchmarking: a short trace sample and their collection of p95/p99 under production envelope.

Proposed Redwood-run test plan (high level):
1) Lightweight synthetic probe (sanity): 1–2 days, low-risk, confirm API semantics and routing.
2) Shadow/parallel traffic window: 1 week of controlled traffic to collect p95/p99 with your payloads.
3) Focused stress windows: 2–4 hours for concurrency and streaming edge cases (we'll coordinate exact times).

We typically need a sample trace and an export of the incumbent provider's 95/99 numbers to baseline. I attached a small demo-trace-sample.txt from today for reference.

Suggested calendar items:
- Technical deep dive (engineers): Jan 11, 10:00am PT — confirm?
- Shadow test kickoff: week of Jan 15 (flexible based on your ops windows).

If you can confirm the p95/p99 targets you need and share the incumbent summary, we can scope the test matrix and provide a preliminary timeline and cost estimate.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: demo-trace-sample.txt (text)

From: Evan Park <evan.park@clearguide.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Clara Gomez <clara.gomez@clearguide.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarifying p95/p99 targets and test scope

Thanks, Olga — useful recap. A few specifics from our side to help scope tests: 

Baseline (what we see from incumbent, end-to-end across our network):
- p95: ~220 ms
- p99: ~620 ms
- Typical sustained QPS: 40
- Peak burst QPS: 150 (spikes during onboarding flows)
- Average request size: 300 tokens; occasional long requests up to 2,400 tokens (prompt + response).

Target we'd like from Redwood if we migrated or routed:
- p95 <= 200 ms end-to-end
- p99 <= 550 ms end-to-end

Streaming details:
- We use chunked streaming for interactive sessions: average chunk ~40 tokens every 60–120ms on sender side; average session concurrency ~6–12 simultaneous streaming sessions per user-facing node.
- We rely on keep-alive connections; abrupt connection drops lead to degraded UX.

Other notes:
- We can provide an "incumbent-performance-summary.pdf" with traces and the raw time-series (attached).
- Security: we will use a staging API key for any probe; no PII in probe payloads.

Happy to do the deep-dive on Jan 11 at 10am PT. For the shadow test, week of Jan 15 works. Preferred window for a short stress test is Jan 18 02:00–06:00 PT (low customer activity).

—Evan
Evan Park
Head of Platform
ClearGuide

Attachments: incumbent-performance-summary.pdf (pdf)

Evan — thanks for the numbers, that's very helpful. Two quick operational asks from our side before the stress window:

1) Can you confirm whether the staging key we'll use should be scoped to a single region or global? Region scoping will change routing and baseline latency expectations.
2) Are you ok with Redwood creating a temporary canary route (5% of test traffic) and returning metrics to you every 30 minutes during the shadow run? We'll keep the payloads non-production-safe (no PII) as noted.

Cost note: the planned shadow + stress windows will generate a modest token volume; I can share a preliminary cost estimate after we finalize expected concurrency and token sizes.

If Jan 18 02:00–06:00 PT is acceptable, we'll schedule the stress window for that slot and put the canary route in place 24 hours before.
